transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I can plan everything out in detail, but when it’s time to actually sit down and do the work, I just can’t seem to make myself stick with it for more than a few minutes. It's really starting to hold me back from getting my career and applications on track.

Have you had problems with focus, staying organized, or finishing tasks since childhood, like in school, or did this mostly start recently? Also, do you feel down or lose interest in things most days?

Looking back, this actually goes back to childhood—I'd constantly forget worksheets, leave projects to the last minute, and get report cards calling me "bright but careless," though it's become a major roadblock over the last two years. As for my mood, I'm definitely frustrated and feel stuck because of these struggles, but I haven't lost interest in my passions like art history or felt depressed.
When you were a child, did these attention and follow-through problems happen in more than one place, like both at school and at home? Can you give one example from each if so?

Yes, it definitely happened in both settings. At school, I would often miss easy questions or skip parts of assignments, which led to report card comments like "bright but careless." Meanwhile, at home, I would constantly forget to bring the right worksheets back with me and completely lose track of long-term projects until the night before they were due, causing a lot of stress.
Do these attention and follow-through problems still affect more than one part of your life now, such as work or school, home responsibilities, or relationships? Can you give one current example?

Yes, they absolutely affect multiple areas of my life. I'm currently unemployed and unable to get my career started because I keep stalling on my grad school and internship applications. At the same time, it's causing a lot of tension at home with my parents, who are really frustrated by my lack of follow-through.

Besides the focus and follow-through problems, do you also have symptoms like feeling restless, fidgety, talking excessively, interrupting others, or acting before thinking? If so, did those also start in childhood?

I do tend to talk excessively, often rambling on about museum politics or obscure art until I notice people's eyes glazing over, but I don't really experience physical restlessness or impulsivity. Even when I was a kid, my struggles were strictly focused on inattention and disorganization—like forgetting worksheets and making careless mistakes—rather than any physical hyperactivity.

Have these attention problems caused clear problems in at least two settings throughout your life, like school/work and home, even during times when you were otherwise not especially stressed or anxious? Also, have any teachers, parents, or others noticed and commented on these problems over the years?

Yes, they have caused ongoing issues both at school and now at home, leaving me unemployed and living with my parents, which has created a lot of tension. Others have definitely noticed; my elementary school teachers wrote "bright but careless" on my report cards, my parents constantly ask why I can't follow through, and a campus mentor recently urged me to seek help.

final_diagnosis.reason: Lifelong pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood, present across school and home and continuing to impair current functioning in work/career and family life. Symptoms include careless mistakes, forgetfulness, disorganization, poor follow-through, and procrastination on sustained tasks, without evidence that depression better explains the presentation. Hyperactive symptoms are minimal, supporting predominantly inattentive ADHD.
